## Title

**Anatomic Concordance Detects Broken Bulk-RNA Deconvolution: No Method Recovers the Lymphoid Compartment in Two Glioma Cohorts**

*Both clauses of the registered question are named. Clause 1 — can anatomy stand in for ground truth when choosing a method? — is answered by `Detects`, with the colon carrying what it cannot do. Clause 2 — does a method that gets the anatomy right also get the biology right? — is answered `no`, categorically, by the pre-registered T > B criterion.*

*A caution for anyone shortening this. An earlier draft read "the best-scoring method inverts the lymphoid compartment". That is false: the best-scoring method is `music`, which returns exactly zero T, NK and B in 55 of 56 GBM and 443 of 510 LGG samples — absence, not inversion. "Top methods invert" is defensible (3 of the top 5 do, in both cohorts) but invites exactly that check. `No method recovers` makes no claim about any single method and is the stronger statement anyway.*

*D23 caution (2026-10-01). `No Method Recovers` holds as **no method robustly recovers**: on the registered signature 0 of 12 (GBM) and 0 of 12 (LGG) order T above B; on the donor-level raw/X rebuild 3 of 14 and 2 of 13 do -- one by returning its reference's own composition, the others weakly or fragilely. If a reviewer presses, `No Method Robustly Recovers` is the exact form.*

*Truth check (GIMiCC, 2026-10-03): INCONCLUSIVE by its registered rule (§4.4). A glioma-specific methylation method agrees with EpiDISH in GBM (T above B, every control passing) and disagrees in LGG (B above T). The GBM truth is corroborated three ways; the LGG truth is contested -- state the lymphoid headline for GBM, and for LGG only with that caveat.*

*Alternatives, if a reviewer wants a different angle foregrounded:* "Bulk RNA deconvolution cannot report the lymphoid compartment of a glioma" (capability angle) or "Two independent ground truths show bulk RNA deconvolution fails on the immune compartment of glioma, and no ground-truth-free check detects it" (method-comparison angle).

## Abstract

Reference-based deconvolution estimates cell-type proportions from bulk RNA expression, and is applied where direct measurement by single-cell sequencing is not available. Selecting among the available methods, however, requires known composition — the measurement deconvolution is used in place of. We tested whether pre-specified anatomic constraints can serve as a selection criterion in its absence. Cell-composition orderings between the anatomic regions of glioblastoma, predicted from neuropathology and independent of any deconvolution algorithm, were hashed and publicly registered before any method was scored. Fifteen estimators and two negative controls were then ranked by the fraction of constraints satisfied, termed the Anatomic Concordance Score (ACS). ACS separated the lowest-scoring fully evaluable estimator from the highest-scoring control by 0.31 on a 0–1 scale, and both controls failed their own within-tumour permutation nulls. The ACS ordering did not, however, predict accuracy against DNA-derived tumour purity, an orthogonal measurement sharing no input with the anatomic arm (Spearman ρ = 0.081, n = 12, p = 0.80); the pre-registered threshold was met only against a synthetic yardstick constructed from the same single-cell atlas used for deconvolution. Against DNA methylation, no method reproduced the T-cell-over-B-cell ordering that methylation resolves robustly across reference builds: 0 of 12 did so on the registered signature, in glioblastoma and again in an independent lower-grade glioma cohort, and on a donor-level rebuild the one method to do so consistently returned its single-cell reference's own composition -- against a prediction registered before those data were analysed. Concordance with established biology is therefore not evidence that a composition estimate is quantitatively correct.

## I. Introduction

> WRITE. Four beats, in this order. Everything below is a fact or a citation to build on, not a sentence to keep.

> **1 · Why composition matters clinically.** The proportion of T cells, macrophages and vasculature in a tumour predicts response to immunotherapy. One or two sentences; this is the only part a clinical reader needs.

> **2 · Why deconvolution exists — the cost argument.** Single-cell sequencing measures composition directly and costs on the order of thousands of dollars per sample, plus instruments and staff most hospitals do not have. Bulk RNA-seq is already routine and a fraction of the price; deconvolution recovers composition from it computationally, with no extra tissue and no extra instrument. **Cite a current per-sample figure rather than asserting `expensive` — this project holds no costing artefact, so the number must come from a source you cite [3].** This is the equity argument: if deconvolution is trustworthy, tumour immune profiling becomes available anywhere bulk sequencing already is.

> **3 · The circularity.** Dozens of methods exist and they disagree. Choosing between them conventionally needs ground truth — the expensive measurement. Benchmarks lean on simulated mixtures or flow cytometry [1][2][3], and rankings derived from simulated bulk do not transfer to real bulk [4]. So the labs that most need deconvolution are the least able to validate it.

> **4 · What this study does about it.** Glioblastoma has pathologist-named anatomic regions with cell-composition gradients that are textbook and independent of any algorithm [5]. Scoring a method on whether it reproduces them needs a slide and a label, not a cell count. State the question in the registered form: *can a tumour's own anatomy stand in for ground truth when choosing a method — and does a method that gets the anatomy right also get the biology right?*

## III. Statistical Analysis, Data Analysis and Measurements

> WRITE: beats and facts below; compose the prose. Every figure here is verified in `docs/STATISTICAL_VERIFICATION.md`, which recomputed each one from the underlying data and, where a statistic rests on an approximation, checked it against an exact or permutation alternative.

**The measurement.** The Anatomic Concordance Score is the fraction of pre-registered constraint/tumour pairs a method satisfies. Constraints are cell-composition orderings between anatomic regions that a neuropathologist would predict; they were fixed and hashed before any method was scored (`ivygap/anatomic/constraints.py`).

| quantity | test | null | n |
|---|---|---|---|
| Anatomic Concordance Score | fraction of constraint/tumour pairs satisfied | **within-tumour permutation** of structure labels, 10,000 draws | 122 samples, 9 evaluable tumours |
| ACS vs accuracy | Spearman rank correlation over methods | pre-registered bar ρ ≥ 0.60 **and** a bootstrap CI excluding zero | 9–14 methods |
| confidence intervals | percentile bootstrap resampling **methods**, 5,000 draws, seed fixed in `config.RANDOM_SEED` | — | as above |
| tumour-content recovery | `1 + slope` of (estimate − truth) regressed on truth | 0 = no information, 1 = perfect | 147 GBM / 496 LGG |
| lymphoid ordering | two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank, **paired within sample** | — | 56 GBM / 510 LGG per method |
| per-sample model fit | R² of the best non-negative fit | floor = shuffled gene→type labels; ceiling = top-8 SVD | 175 GBM / 534 LGG |

> **1 · Why the null is a permutation, not a coin flip.** Cell fractions are compositional and correlated, so a 50% null is wrong. Structure labels are permuted **within** each tumour, which preserves both the tumour's composition and the structure sizes. State this explicitly — it is the difference between a real null and a decorative one.

> **2 · Two negative controls, and why they license every claim.** One method receives random cell proportions; the other a signature matrix with its gene labels shuffled. A scorer that rates real and broken inputs alike measures nothing, and you cannot discover that by looking at real inputs alone. Report the margin.

> **3 · Nesting.** Samples are nested within tumours, so all scoring collapses to (tumour, structure) before aggregation. Say so; a reviewer will check.

> **4 · What was excluded, and on what rule.** Methods run without an input their published algorithm requires are marked *degenerate* or *not comparable* by declared rule (`ivygap/deconv/comparability.py`), before any score is seen. Distinguish **could not be evaluated** from **evaluated and wrong** — quanTIseq is the first, not the second.

> **5 · How the statistics were checked.** p-values come from an asymptotic t-approximation, which is worth distrusting at n = 9–14. Each was compared against a permutation p computed on ranks — exact by full enumeration at n = 9 (362,880 permutations), Monte-Carlo above. No difference exceeded 0.004, and the registered outcome clears the bar under either calculation. Both bootstrap intervals reproduce bit-for-bit from the recorded seed.

> **6 · Reporting convention for permutation p-values.** With 10,000 draws the smallest attainable p is 1/10001. Values at that floor are reported as **p < 1e-4**, never as a point estimate, because the test cannot resolve finer.

### 4.2 · Anatomic concordance does not identify a method that is biologically correct

This is the second clause of the registered question, tested directly against the pre-registered criterion rather than through the underpowered rank correlation above.

| | GBM | LGG |
|---|---|---|
| methods reproducing the registered **T > B** | **0 of 12** | **0 of 12** |
| method ranked **first** by anatomic concordance | `music`, ACS 0.9692 | `music`, ACS 0.9692 |
| …does it get T > B right? | **no** | **no** |
| …fraction of samples it places **B above T** | **100.0%** | **98.5%** |

**In every cohort tested, ZERO methods reproduce the pre-registered T > B ordering, and the method ranked FIRST by anatomic concordance is among the failures. Anatomic concordance therefore cannot be used to choose a method that gets the lymphoid compartment right, because no such method is present at any concordance level. This claim is categorical and needs no correlation.**

> WRITE: this is the study's registered null — *"the answer matches known biology" is not evidence that the answer is right* — demonstrated outright. Rest it HERE, not on the rank correlation in Result 1, which is underpowered and cannot carry it. State the timestamp: the prediction preceded the measurement by ninety-five minutes and named its own falsifier.

**What must NOT be claimed.** The rank correlation between anatomic concordance and lymphoid failure runs *opposite* to the hypothesis — GBM +0.45 (p = 0.14), LGG +0.48 (p = 0.12) on 12 methods — but it is **not significant** and must be reported as directional only, if at all. The categorical finding above needs no correlation.

| | GBM *(discovery)* | LGG *(registered replication)* |
|---|---|---|
| methylation truth T : NK : B | 0.5224 : 0.3678 : 0.1098 | 0.4758 : 0.3208 : 0.2034 |
| T ranked first, per sample | 63.6% | 79.2% |

| samples compared | 56 | 510 |
| **methods agreeing T > B** | **0 of 12** | **0 of 12** |

**Two failure modes, counted separately — do not merge them.**

- **ABSENCE.** 4 of 12 (GBM) and 4 of 12 (LGG) methods return **exactly 0.0000** for T, B *and* NK in the majority of samples. `music`/`nnls`: 443 of 510 LGG samples, 55 of 56 GBM. Verified as exact zeros, not small values.
- **MISASSIGNMENT.** Of the methods that do report lymphocytes, **8 of 8** (LGG) and **6 of 8** (GBM) place B above T on a majority of the samples they score, paired within sample. Discordance with methylation reaches 94.6% (LGG, `elastic_net`) and 100.0% (GBM, `elastic_net`).

> WRITE: the pre-registration named the falsifier in advance — *"methylation showing B ≥ T ... the anomaly withdrawn"*. Quote it. A prediction that could have killed the finding and did not is worth more than the result stated flat.

> WRITE: say plainly that reporting *no lymphocytes at all* in a glioma is a worse failure than reversing the T:B ratio, and that it was invisible while the comparison was made on cohort means. That correction is part of the result.

**Is the truth itself right? (exploratory, post-registration).** The ordering above is EpiDISH's, from a blood reference into which brain and tumour DNA can only be forced. GIMiCC [52], a methylation method built for glioma, separates tumour, neuronal, glial and angiogenic DNA before it splits the lymphocytes (`prespecified/gimicc_truth_confirmation.md`). Its registered reading is **INCONCLUSIVE**: the shuffled-CpG negative control in LGG failed. Measured: its tumour layer tracks ABSOLUTE purity (Spearman 0.9351 GBM, 0.6302 LGG), its immune total tracks the methylation leukocyte fraction (0.9592, 0.9208), with shuffled CpG labels its tumour layer tracks purity at -0.1158 (GBM) and 0.648 (LGG; the control requires |rho| < 0.20), and the direction holds in 18 and 19 of 20 repeats that drop a further 20% of its CpGs. Within-lymphoid T : NK : B is 0.462 : 0.261 : 0.277 in GBM -- **T above B, with every GBM control passing** -- and 0.405 : 0.102 : 0.493 in LGG: **B above T**, against EpiDISH's T > NK > B in both.

Diagnostics declared before they were computed (exploratory) locate both results. Shuffling CpG labels reverses each ordering (B>NK>T in GBM, T>NK>B in LGG), so both are carried by the lymphoid CpGs themselves, not by global methylation. LGG's B excess is not tumour signal absorbed into B: GIMiCC's B share falls as purity rises (Spearman -0.145, p 0.003). The LGG negative control fails by construction: GIMiCC's IDH-mutant purity libraries consist almost entirely of tumour-hypermethylated CpGs, so a shuffled LGG sample reads its global methylation (Spearman 0.92 with mean beta), which tracks purity. **In LGG, two methylation instruments disagree on T versus B.**

GIMiCC zeroes or drops level-4 T where its CD4/CD8 projection is undefined (0 GBM and 6 LGG samples); taking T straight from its lymphoid layer gives T>B>NK (GBM) and B>T>NK (LGG). Per sample, the two methylation instruments barely agree: GIMiCC's and EpiDISH's T shares correlate at Spearman 0.08 (GBM) and 0.11 (LGG).

Re-scored against GIMiCC's direction, the methods matching it number 0 of 12 and 12 of 12 on the frozen signature, 3 of 14 and 11 of 13 on the raw/X reference: the headline is **reversed for TCGA-LGG** under the second instrument -- a reading that inherits GIMiCC's own INCONCLUSIVE status.

D23's reference-free positive control, which EpiDISH's per-sample split failed, gives for GIMiCC's per-sample T/(T+B) Spearman +0.185 (p 0.151, n 62, GBM) and +0.100 (p 0.0351, n 433, LGG): **FAILS** -- so methylation remains a cohort-level truth only, under either instrument.

Against GIMiCC's lymphoid tissue fraction (denominators matched by construction), E2's lymphoid estimate gives Spearman +0.65 / +0.08 (GBM, `unmix` / methods' median) and +0.53 / -0.25 (LGG). By the rule fixed beforehand, the claim that the lymphoid estimate does not track methylation **does not hold** against a second methylation truth for `unmix`, whose tracking survives controlling for the leukocyte fraction (partial +0.36 / +0.32), so it is more than the leukocyte level; the methods' median does not track (+0.12 / -0.05 partial).

**Direct cell counts, with no methylation and no deconvolution.** In an independent single-cell atlas (Abdelfattah et al. [42], 18 patients, not one of GBmap's source studies), the T/NK cluster split per cell by the split declared before (`prespecified/atlas_t_vs_b.md`) gives 17,311 T, 1,302 NK and 1,205 B cells; T exceeds B in 18 of 18 patients: **SUPPORTS T > B**. GBmap's own core atlas (all glioblastoma) holds 54,257 T against 1,250 B cells, T above B in 96 of 98 donors with any lymphocytes. Flow cytometry of brain tumours reports the same composition: "the lymphocyte compartment was mostly composed of T cells with fewer NK cells and B cells" [53].

**Reading.** In glioblastoma, the discovery cohort, the truth is corroborated three ways -- a glioma-specific methylation instrument with every control passing, two single-cell atlases, and flow cytometry -- and the headline stands on it. In LGG, the registered replication, the methylation truth depends on the instrument: the deconvolution methods' B above T agrees with GIMiCC and disagrees with EpiDISH, while the direct counts (two LGG patients in the atlas, and pooled flow cytometry) favour T above B. Both methylation instruments place B above every direct count (GIMiCC several-fold), so T > B is a fact about glioma tissue, and the methylation shares are not measurements of it at that precision. **The LGG replication of the lymphoid finding rests on a contested truth; the GBM discovery does not.**

### 4.5 · The additive mixing model accounts for a minority of real bulk

> **[ FIGURE 6 HERE ]** — `docs/figures/Figure_model_fit_bound.pdf` (vector, for submission) / `.png` (300 dpi, for drafts). Per-sample fit of the non-negative mixing model, against floor and ceiling controls. Caption in `docs/FIGURES.md`.

| | GBM | LGG |
|---|---|---|
| R² of best additive fit (median) | 0.3621 | 0.236 |
| variance unexplained (%) | 63.79 | 76.4 |
| samples below R² = 0.5 | 0.8286 | 0.8914 |
| floor: gene labels shuffled per type | -0.0077 | -0.0071 |
| floor: random non-negative basis | 0.0016 | 0.0016 |
| ceiling: top-8 SVD of the bulk | 0.9803 | 0.9904 |
| **reference as fraction of achievable** | 0.3892 | 0.2499 |

**Five explanations proposed and rejected, each with a working control:**

1. **Signature cannot separate T from B** — refuted. On mixtures built from the reference itself, NNLS recovers the planted ratio (2.333) exactly, survives 100% multiplicative noise, and survives deleting an entire cell type. Condition number **5.29**.
2. **Macrophage spillover into B** — rejected. 5 of 10 methods, sign-test p **0.623047**.
3. **High tumour purity explains the absence mode** — rejected. 2 of 8 (GBM) and 1 of 8 (LGG) methods; several run the opposite way.
4. **Per-sample model fit as a trust signal** — rejected. 1 of 12 (GBM) and 6 of 12 (LGG), with 2 LGG methods significant in the **wrong** direction. The control passes (R² is not a purity proxy), which is what makes the negative meaningful.
5. **Residual propagation through correlated columns** — rejected. Refitting on lymphoid-owned markers only gives T > B in **0.0%** of samples; the mass moves to NK.
6. **The `NK_cell` column absorbs T-cell signal through shared CD3 markers** — rejected. The frozen reference was re-annotated and refit, with the gene space held fixed and the as-registered fit reproducing the registered estimates exactly. With the NK column **removed**, SVR places B above T in **100%** (GBM) and **100%** (LGG) of samples with lymphoid signal; with T and NK **merged**, in **100%** and **100%** (NNLS: 100% and 100% in LGG). Whatever the roster does with NK, the mass goes to B, never to T. `results/nk_reannotation.json`.
7. **Immunoglobulin transcripts credited to B** — excluded by construction: the solved gene space holds 1 immunoglobulin gene (JCHAIN), 0.057% of the B column.
8. **Ribosomal-protein genes admitted as B markers** — rejected. They carry 62% of the B column's mass in the solved space (T 20%) and most of its pull in a residual-driver analysis, yet removing them leaves B above T in 100% of GBM samples under SVR (baseline 90%) and 100% in LGG. `results/ribosomal_test.json`.
9. **Ambient myelin RNA in the B profile** — rejected: GBmap's B cells carry *less* myelin signal than its T cells (24% vs 39% of cells with any). `results/atlas_cell_fractions.json`.

**Measured properties of the B column — not shown to cause the inversion.** Its profile is the most bulk-tissue-like lymphoid profile (correlation with the mean GBM bulk 0.3448 vs T 0.1523, NK 0.1443; the order holds without ribosomal genes); removing the column under SVR sends 92% of its estimate to Tumor and 16% to T in GBM; GBmap's B cells carry a median 42% of their molecules in ribosomal genes (T 26%).
The reabsorption is estimator-specific: under NNLS the removed B mass goes to T instead (182% in GBM, 109% in LGG, with Tumor falling), while under SVR in LGG 99% goes to Tumor, as in GBM; so B behaves as an overflow for tumour signal under SVR and as a competitor of T under NNLS, in both cohorts. The SVR pattern motivated the hypothesis BayesPrism's sample-specific tumour model (key = "Tumor") tests (§4.10, prediction fixed before output).

**An independent atlas (pre-specified).** The reference was rebuilt from Abdelfattah et al. 2022 (GSE182109) -- not one of GBmap's 16 source studies -- with B cells from 16 patients rather than GBmap's concentrated few, clusters named by a marker rule fixed before any expression was seen (`prespecified/abdelfattah_cluster_mapping.md`). Its B column carries plasma cells, so immunoglobulin genes dominate it; an immunoglobulin-removed refit was declared before the result. GBM SVR: GBmap B>NK>T (B>T 90%) -> independent atlas B>T>NK (B>T 89%), Ig removed B>T>NK (B>T 86%); GBM NNLS: GBmap B>NK>T (B>T 100%) -> independent atlas B>T>NK (B>T 69%), Ig removed B>T>NK (B>T 40%); LGG SVR: GBmap B>NK>T (B>T 96%) -> independent atlas B>T>NK (B>T 84%), Ig removed B>T>NK (B>T 64%); LGG NNLS: GBmap B>NK>T (B>T 99%) -> independent atlas T>B>NK (B>T 5%), Ig removed T>B>NK (B>T 20%).
Read as pre-specified, the result is **mixed** across methods, cohorts or the immunoglobulin sensitivity; each cell above is reported as measured and none is promoted. `results/independent_atlas_test*.json`.
The immunoglobulin-removed refit, declared before the result was seen, gives the same cohort-level ordering in all 4 cohort-method cells, so by the declared reading immunoglobulin content does not drive it; removal costs resolution (fewer samples keep any lymphoid signal), not direction.
Rebuilt with three further cell-sampling seeds (a check declared after the main result, so it can only qualify it), GBM SVR, LGG NNLS, LGG SVR keep their ordering in every build; GBM NNLS does not, and loses its reading. `results/independent_atlas_seed_sensitivity.json`.

### 4.6 · Reference parity, and what it changes

- **Replicates:** MuSiC moves from excluded-as-arithmetically-NNLS to **rank 1** given the cross-donor variance it is designed to use (GBM 17.5% → 60.2%; LGG 20.0% → 52.6%). A method that could not previously be measured at all.
- **Replicates:** the lymphoid trade-off. Methods agreeing on T > B go 0/12 → 3/14 (GBM) and 0/12 → 2/13 (LGG), while methods returning zero lymphoid content go 4/12 → 6/14 and 4/12 → 7/13. Misassignment partly repairs; absence worsens.
- **Replicates:** equal footing makes the absolute under-call **worse** — GBM median bias -0.0277 → -0.4767, methods under-calling 7/12 → 14/14. (The two arms score different-sized panels, 12 and 14, because equal footing makes more methods runnable.)
- **DOES NOT REPLICATE:** the ranking reshuffle. Kendall tau **+0.214** (GBM) and **+0.333** (LGG); but excluding the one method whose implementation also changed gives **+0.143** (GBM, effect intact) and **+0.733** (LGG, rankings largely agree). Six to seven methods per tau. **Report as a partial replication failure.**

### 4.7 · Genuine packages versus reimplementations

_Re-measured 2026-09-30 on the leaderboard's own atlas layer (`raw/X`), gene space, donor split and sample order -- eight input-equivalence conditions, the eighth being the matrix layer. `results/{bisque,epic,dwls,bayesprism}_remeasured.json`._

> **Correction (OPEN_DEFECTS D22).** Every earlier re-measurement ran on GBmap's log-transformed `X` layer while the leaderboard ran on genuine counts, because the script never passed the layer and the builder defaults to `X`. Bisque's earlier 0.9231 and EPIC's 0.9846 equal their log-arm leaderboard values to four decimals. The deltas previously reported in this section were cross-matrix, not cross-implementation, and are withdrawn; the superseded artefacts are kept in `results/superseded_D22/`.

| method | leaderboard row is | leaderboard ACS | genuine package, raw/X | samples estimated | constraint pairs | runtime |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `bisque` | R:BisqueRNA | 0.7077 | **0.7077** [0.5972, 0.8167] | 122 of 122 | 57 | 18 s |
| `epic` | R:EPIC | 0.7692 | **0.7692** [0.6567, 0.8788] | 122 of 122 | 57 | 17 s |
| `dwls` | python-reimplementation | 0.7231 | **0.7000** [0.5588, 0.9130] | 49 of 122 | 26 | 2,099 s |
| `bayesprism` | python-reimplementation | 0.8000 | **0.8154** [0.6999, 0.9286] | 122 of 122 | 57 | 16,523 s |

**Bisque and EPIC reproduce their leaderboard rows exactly.** Both rows already were the genuine packages, so this is a determinism check passing -- the same package on the same inputs returns the same number -- and it is *not* evidence that a reimplementation agrees with a package.

**Genuine DWLS cannot be compared on this cohort.** On the counts layer the package's solver returned no estimate for **73 of 122** samples, so its ACS of 0.7000 rests on 26 constraint pairs from 6 tumours, against the reimplementation's full cohort. The failures are inside the package's quadratic program (*"constraints are inconsistent, no solution!"*), and an independent re-run reproduced them exactly. On the log layer the same package estimated every sample. A method whose output depends on which layer of the same atlas it is given, to the point of failing on most samples, is a finding about the method; a delta between its partial ACS and a complete one is not.

**Genuine BayesPrism is the one clean genuine-versus-reimplementation comparison.** On the counts layer, with every input equivalent and all 122 samples estimated, the package scores 0.8154 [0.6999, 0.9286] against the reimplementation's 0.8000 -- a difference of +0.0154, inside the package's interval. It needed 4.6 h of R time on this machine with no budget, against the confirmatory run's 2,400 s; that budget, not the method, is why the leaderboard row is the reimplementation.

**Whether a row is the published package can depend on machine state.** BayesPrism's `parallel` socket cluster spawns worker processes, each with its own copy of the data, and on an 8 GB machine they can be killed (`Error in unserialize(node$con)`); DWLS's runtime sits close to its 2,400 s budget. Either can silently become the reimplementation depending on free memory and load, which is not a scientific variable. `docs/OPEN_DEFECTS.md` D18, D19, D22.

> WRITE: a reproducibility finding, not a limitation footnote. Two of fifteen methods could become different software depending on machine state, and the re-measurement meant to settle it was itself confounded by an unpassed argument until an eighth equivalence check was added. Any benchmark that does not record the atlas layer has the same exposure.

### 4.8 · Biological factors associated with estimation error

- **Mesenchymal character** predicts a larger under-call in GBM. **Does not replicate in LGG** — the Verhaak class does not exist there and the expression-score surrogate is null. Report as cohort-specific; do **not** headline it.
- **Genomic instability does not predict error**: ploidy, whole-genome doubling, subclonal fraction all null in both cohorts, at equal prominence.

### 4.9 · Spatial distribution of the mesenchymal program (exploratory)

MES score across five Ivy GAP niches is monotone with the hypoxic perinecrotic zone highest. **The pre-specified test is not significant (p = 0.3312)** — the statistic was "which structure is the maximum", weak at five categories. Post hoc: PAN − LE positive in 6 of 6 tumours, p = 0.0142, trend r = +0.957. **Suggestive, not established.**

The prediction does not replicate. In LGG the authors' configuration RAISES B's share (higher in 390 of 510 samples, median +0.215). Modelling each tumour's own expression is therefore not a general account of B's excess. B stays above T under both configurations in both cohorts.

**Two truth-free rankings of ReCIDE, adjudicated by DNA (exploratory; rule fixed before the run, `prespecified/recide_tcga.md`).** ReCIDE has the lowest anatomic ACS of any real method here (0.692). Li et al. 2026 [4], its developers, single it out with BayesPrism as robust on truth-free reproducibility. On TCGA-GBM's raw/X arm, ReCIDE's tumour content ranks 8 of 9 against DNA purity (rho 0.522), in the bottom third: anatomy's low ranking agrees with DNA here, and the reproducibility ranking does not. The other method they singled out, genuine BayesPrism, ranks first and third of 9 (its two configurations). This is one method and one cohort, so it is a single observation, not a test. In TCGA-LGG, outside the rule and descriptive only, it ranks 9 of 9 (rho 0.316).

**The agreement test with the extension methods added (exploratory).** The methods with both an anatomic ACS and a TCGA purity correlation (aric, deseq2_unmix, fardeep, lindeconseq, mixture) raise the panel to n = 17: rho = +0.285 (permutation p = 0.27, 95% CI -0.24 to +0.70), against the registered +0.081 (n = 12, reproduced). Still below the registered bar of 0.60; and because these methods were added after the registered result was known, the number is reported, not tested. `results/extension/agreement_extended.json`.

> WRITE: one paragraph. These methods widen the panel; they cannot widen the registered agreement test, whose n is fixed by registration. A high ACS for a post-registration method is reported, never used to rank -- the study's own finding is that ACS does not predict accuracy.

### 4.11 · Independent checks of the yardstick and of ACS

_Analyses completed during the study that had not reached the manuscript (recovered 2026-10-01). Each is exploratory; none moves the frozen constraint file or a registered statistic._

**The registered constraints hold in measurements that involve no deconvolution.**
- *Spatially resolved single-cell composition* (Mossa Albiach et al. 2023; one patient, 27 samples): **3 of 4** testable constraints satisfied (C1, C2, C7; C1 by 13.34-fold, p 5e-05). C5 violated -- tested on Albiach's necrotic core, which is not Ivy GAP's peri-necrotic rim where macrophages accumulate, so the test sits on the wrong side of that boundary. n = 1 patient: within-tumour replication only.
- *FACS-gated single-cell data* (Darmanis et al. 2017; 4 patients, 3,589 cells): C1 (tumour higher in core than periphery) supported in **4 of 4** sorting gates, 2 at p < 0.05 -- the only cross-patient test of a constraint.
- *Ivy GAP in situ hybridisation* (42 donors, 899 sub-blocks; markers declared before reading values): the well-sampled markers support the constraints -- CD44 for C1 (p 0.0005, 137 sub-blocks); BIRC5 for C1 (p 0.0070, 134 sub-blocks); CD44 for C7 (p 0.0005, 112 sub-blocks); BIRC5 for C7 (p 0.0160, 109 sub-blocks). 18 marker tests rest on fewer than 50 sub-blocks and are reported in `results/ish_constraint_check.json` without weight. C2 cannot be checked: the ISH panel has no oligodendrocyte-lineage marker.

**A pre-registered protein-level test: ACS reversed the ground-truth ordering.** Ajaib et al. 2023 scored one algorithm (MCPcounter) with different marker sets against imaging mass cytometry on matched tissue; GBM-specific markers tracked protein-measured immune content far better than GBmap-derived markers (r = 0.37 vs 0.06). The prediction registered before scoring (`prespecified/imc_anchored_prediction.md`) was that ACS would order them the same way. It did not: ACS **0.5128** for the GBM-specific set against **0.6667** for the GBmap set, on the same 31 constraint pairs -- and at a matched marker density of 79 per type the GBmap set falls to 0.3846, so even the reversed ordering is unstable. A third, protein-level instrument therefore agrees with the DNA arms: anatomic concordance does not rank.

**ACS is not an AUC, and an AUC does not rescue it (exploratory).** ACS thresholds: each constraint-tumour pair scores 1 or 0 on per-structure means. Its graded counterpart -- the within-tumour Mann-Whitney AUC over the same pairs, samples and permutation null (`scripts/anatomic_auc.py`) -- ranks the 14 comparable estimators almost identically (Spearman rho = 0.94) but on a different scale: chance is 0.50 for the AUC and 0.37 for ACS (median permutation-null means), and the AUC gives partial credit on the two conjunction constraints (C4, C7) where ACS gives none, so an ACS and an AUC of the same value do not mean the same thing. Both measure agreement with anatomy; neither sees ground truth. Substituted for ACS in the registered agreement test, the AUC predicts DNA-measured accuracy no better: rho = -0.06 against ABSOLUTE purity (p = 0.85, n = 12; registered ACS rho = +0.081), and -0.004 against purity re-expressed as a concordance on the same 0.5-chance scale. The null result is not an artefact of ACS's thresholding. `results/anatomic_auc.json`.

> **[ FIGURE 9 HERE ]** — `docs/figures/Figure_acs_vs_auc.pdf`. (A) ACS against the within-tumour AUC, with each statistic's chance level; (B) the AUC against concordance with DNA-measured purity. Exploratory; caption in `docs/FIGURES.md`.

**The constraints can be met without any single-cell reference.** CDSeq, a reference-free method, estimates components from the bulk alone; named by correlation with GBmap profiles it reaches ACS 0.8462 (permutation p < 1e-4, 57 pairs), named by independent GBM markers 0.6829 (p 0.0009, 41 pairs). Detection does not depend on the atlas.

A second reference-free method of a different kind, Linseed [51] (simplex corners of mutually linear genes, where CDSeq is a topic model; k fixed at 8 as for CDSeq, post-registration, `prespecified/linseed_config.md`), also meets the constraints, though less well: ACS 0.6769 profile-named (permutation p < 1e-4) and 0.6585 marker-named (p 0.0056). On TCGA bulk its tumour component tracks ABSOLUTE purity only weakly (Spearman 0.3649 / 0.0892 GBM, 0.2103 / -0.2259 LGG, profile / marker naming), and no labelling claims T, NK and B together, so it yields no lymphoid ordering. The anatomic and TCGA fits are separate deconvolutions; this is descriptive, not a within-fit test of the thesis.

**Total immune content against an independent DNA measurement.** Against the methylation-derived leukocyte fraction of Thorsson et al. 2018 (129 GBM, 510 LGG samples), the pre-registered prediction that methods over-call immune content failed in both cohorts: 2 of 8 methods over-call (sign test p = 0.28906), and the median error is negative (-0.084 GBM, -0.030 LGG). The comparison sets an mRNA share against a cell fraction, which biases toward under-calling, so this is reported as a null, not as an under-call finding. `prespecified/immune_failure_factors.md`.

**The ACS ordering is only partly stable to a change of reference.** Rebuilt from linear GBmap counts, the ACS ordering of 13 methods correlates rho = 0.5099 with the ordering under a reference built from the Neftel 2019 data alone and 0.3655 under Darmanis 2017 alone: about half of the ranking survives. Both datasets are constituents of GBmap, so this bounds the effect of how the reference is assembled, not of a fully independent atlas. (The log-layer comparisons, rho = 0.0379 and 0.1384, are the D16-confounded pair and are not quoted.) An ordering that moves this much with the reference cannot select a method on its own.

**Published benchmarks.** The methods Avila Cobos et al. 2020 place in their top tier on real ground truth in other tissues do not score significantly higher on ACS than the rest (one-sided Mann-Whitney p = 0.125) -- consistent with ACS separating working from broken methods without ranking working ones.

### 4.12 · Which cell types the bulk data determine: a truth-free check (exploratory)

_Post-registration (2026-10-02), rules fixed before computing (`prespecified/identifiability_diagnostics.md`). Motivated by the loss-scale ablation of §4.10, which had already shown the T-versus-B split moving with the loss while tumour content held -- so it is exploratory throughout. It selects nothing and changes no registered statistic. `docs/EXTENSION_IDENTIFIABILITY.md`._

Two diagnostics need no ground truth. **Loss-scale stability** re-fits one genuine package, DESeq2 `unmix` [45], under seven settings of the scale on which its loss is computed (shift 1 to 10,000; power 1 or 2) and asks whether samples keep their order: the mean pairwise Spearman correlation of per-sample estimates across settings. **Method agreement** asks the same across the registered panel. Each was set against an instrument sharing nothing with the RNA: ABSOLUTE purity [7] for tumour content, the methylation-derived leukocyte fraction [8] for all leukocytes, and EpiDISH [12] for the lymphoid total. T, B and NK separately are secondary units, because EpiDISH's per-sample split failed a reference-free positive control.

| compartment | stability, GBM / LGG | method agreement, GBM / LGG | `unmix` vs DNA truth, GBM / LGG | median registered method vs DNA truth, GBM / LGG | samples with truth, GBM / LGG |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tumour (ABSOLUTE) | 0.96 / 0.95 | 0.47 / 0.38 | +0.78 / +0.59 | +0.41 / +0.18 | 154 / 510 |
| All leukocytes (methylation) | 0.95 / 0.93 | 0.56 / 0.35 | +0.78 / +0.60 | +0.49 / +0.08 | 129 / 510 |
| Lymphoid total (EpiDISH) | 0.71 / 0.49 | 0.28 / 0.18 | -0.20 / -0.18 | -0.14 / +0.19 | 56 / 510 |
| T (secondary) | 0.89 / 0.75 | 0.11 / 0.04 | -0.12 / -0.27 | -0.08 / -0.03 | 56 / 510 |
| B (secondary) | 0.52 / 0.47 | 0.26 / 0.20 | +0.09 / -0.00 | -0.13 / +0.08 | 56 / 510 |
| NK (secondary) | 0.70 / 0.74 | 0.09 / 0.06 | -0.12 / -0.07 | +0.00 / -0.03 | 56 / 510 |
| Myeloid, endothelial, oligodendrocyte (no DNA truth) | 0.94-0.99 | 0.47-0.78 | -- | -- | -- |

**Stability ranked the compartments as their agreement with DNA did.** Across the six primary units, loss-scale stability and truth agreement correlate rho = 0.886 (exact one-sided p = 0.0167 over all 720 orderings; pre-declared reading: **SUPPORTED**). Method agreement points the same way, short of significance (rho = 0.657, p = 0.0875). With T, B and NK added (12 units) both are significant (rho = 0.587, p = 0.0242; rho = 0.517, p = 0.0436). Tumour content and total leukocyte content are stable (0.96 / 0.95; 0.95 / 0.93) and track their DNA truths. The lymphoid total is the least stable primary unit in both cohorts (0.71 / 0.49), and `unmix`'s estimate of it does not track EpiDISH (-0.20 / -0.18); across the registered methods the median is -0.14 / +0.19. **The bulk data identify the immune compartment as a whole, not its lymphocyte types.** (Against GIMiCC's lymphoid tissue fraction, a second methylation truth with matched denominators, `unmix`'s lymphoid total does track: +0.65 GBM, +0.53 LGG, §4.4; the methods' median does not. The claim holds for the panel, not for every package.)

**The anatomic constraints sit on the identified compartments.** Every cell type the registered constraints score (endothelial, macrophage/microglia, oligodendrocyte, tumour) is stable under the loss-scale check (0.94-0.99 across both cohorts). T cells were excluded from the constraint file before any output was examined, because "this pipeline's own synthetic benchmark puts T cells at the detection floor, so a T-cell constraint would score noise". The lymphoid compartment is the one this check finds least stable. ACS cannot see the lymphoid failure: it scores no lymphoid contrast, and the compartments it does score are ones the bulk data determine.

**Anatomy does not move toward the right lymphoid answer.** Re-run on the anatomic cohort under the same seven loss settings (Addendum 2, declared before computing; the pre-declared setting reproduces the reported row exactly), `unmix`'s ACS ranges 0.877-0.969. Every setting beats its null, and the pre-declared reading is INCONCLUSIVE (range 0.092, between the bounds of 0.05 and 0.10). Only C6 and C7 change. Descriptively, and not pre-declared: the fits that reproduce methylation's T-above-B ordering in TCGA-GBM score 0.908, 0.877, and the most inverted fits score 0.939, 0.939, 0.969.

`unmix`'s all-leukocyte estimate tracks the methylation leukocyte fraction at rho = 0.780 (GBM) and 0.603 (LGG), above every registered method in both cohorts (best: nu-SVR, 0.688; DWLS (this project's reimplementation), 0.590 -- a margin of 0.013 in LGG, not tested).

**Robustness (post hoc; Addendum 1, written before it was computed).** The two lymphoid units are the two least stable in 100% of 2,000 bootstrap resamples of samples (95% interval of the stability-truth rho 0.54 to 1.00). That contrast alone has null probability 1/15 = 0.067. The rest of the significance comes from the order of the four stable units, whose stability values lie within 0.033 of each other. Swapping the two GBM truth values that differ by 0.0003 gives p = 0.029. The bootstrap holds the six units fixed, so it speaks to sampling, not to how few units there are.

Two flaws in the registered design surfaced after the run; each was checked under a rule written first. (i) In GBM the pre-declared shift is 1, so two of the seven settings are the same fit (byte-identical estimates). Over distinct fits the result is unchanged (rho = 0.886, p = 0.0167). (ii) The method-agreement panel kept Bisque and EPIC, which run in degraded modes here and which the registered immune arm excludes. On that arm's 8-method panel, method agreement tracks truth more closely (rho = 0.771, p = 0.0514), still short of significance.

A third flaw is in the truths themselves. EpiDISH with its blood reference returns shares of the immune compartment, and the registered comparison set them against tissue fractions. On matched denominators (each estimate's share of its own leukocyte total) the lymphoid estimate still does not track EpiDISH (-0.10 / -0.12). It is less stable than before (0.55 / 0.34), and the association strengthens (stability: rho = 0.943, p = 0.0083; method agreement: rho = 0.829, p = 0.0292). The method-agreement figure rests on the samples where every method returns some leukocytes (247 of 510 LGG samples are dropped), so the stability figure is the one to quote.

**Does agreement between methods pick the accurate estimate?** DECEPTICON [46] selects, for each cell type, the two pairs of methods whose estimates correlate most, on the premise that "the most effective analysis strategies for deconvolution demonstrate significant concordance". Its validation used simulations, flow cytometry outside the brain and prognosis. We applied its published rule to the comparable registered methods (this project's code, not the DECEPTICON package; `prespecified/agreement_selection_test.md`). The agreement-selected estimate beat the median of 2,000 randomly paired ensembles in 4 of 6 primary units (reading: INCONCLUSIVE). Across methods, agreement with the other methods tracked agreement with DNA only weakly (mean rho = 0.28, permutation p = 0.035; reading: SUPPORTED). The most-correlated pair was a pair of algorithmic siblings in 9 of 10 selections: nu-SVR with this project's CIBERSORTx-style subclass of it, and NNLS with the BayesPrism reimplementation that iterates it. Their agreement measures shared construction. In LGG the ensemble's leukocyte estimate reached 0.17, no better than random pairs. The most accurate single method (DWLS (this project's reimplementation), 0.59) ranked fifth of 8 by agreement with the others.

**What it does not show.** Stability is evidence, not proof: T cells in GBM are stable (0.89; 0.80 as a share of leukocytes) and do not track EpiDISH (-0.12; -0.01 on matched denominators). That is an estimate that is reproducibly uninformative, the case a reproducibility criterion [4] cannot detect. Part of that stability rests on ties: `unmix` returns exactly zero T in 36% of GBM samples (mean over settings). Stability flags which estimates not to trust; it does not certify the rest. This counter-example depends on the methylation instrument: against GIMiCC's T tissue fraction the same estimate tracks (+0.64 GBM, +0.49 LGG; §4.4), and the two instruments barely agree with each other per sample.
A secondary arm tested the data scale. The pre-declared expectation, from Avila Cobos et al. [1], was that NNLS on log-transformed data would track purity worse than linear NNLS. It failed in both cohorts: rho = 0.715 against 0.562 (GBM) and 0.557 against 0.275 (LGG), on identical inputs without the cell-size conversion. [1] measured level error on simulated mixtures; this arm measures rank agreement on real tumours. The two criteria differ, so this is reported as a contrast, not a refutation.

> **[ FIGURE 11 HERE ]** — `docs/figures/Figure_identifiability.pdf`. Truth-free stability (A, within one package; B, across the registered methods) against agreement with DNA truth, per compartment and cohort.

## V. Discussion

> WRITE: six beats. Facts and citations below; the prose is yours.

> **0 · What is new here, stated before what was found.** Three things, and each is a property of the design rather than a characterisation of the outcome:

>   • **A ground-truth-free benchmark tested against orthogonal molecular truth.** Existing ground-truth-free approaches score *reproducibility* — whether the same cell types shift across cohorts [4]. Reproducibility cannot detect a method that is reproducibly wrong. This study scores *correctness* against two instruments that share no input with the estimator under test: DNA copy number and DNA methylation.

>   • **Negative controls in a deconvolution benchmark.** Two deliberately broken estimators were scored alongside the real ones. The nearest comparable study [4] reports none. **Verify [1][2][3] yourself before generalising this** — only [4] was read in full here. Without a control a score cannot be shown to measure anything. The margin over them is what licenses every claim made here.

>   • **A pre-registered prediction with a named falsifier and a timestamp.** The T > B prediction was committed 95 minutes before the data that tested it existed, together with the outcome that would have withdrawn it. Deconvolution benchmarks are not usually pre-registered at all.

> **And the finding is consequential rather than merely negative.** Immune composition estimated by deconvolution is used to stratify patients and to interpret immunotherapy response. In two glioma cohorts, none of the twelve methods that returned a lymphoid estimate recovered the direction of the T-versus-B relationship that an orthogonal molecular instrument resolves at p < 10⁻²⁴. State the practical reading plainly: a published lymphoid fraction for a glioma cannot be relied upon without an orthogonal measurement, and no internal diagnostic tested here substitutes for one.

> **1 · What the study answers.** Both clauses of the registered question, in the order registered. Anatomy *detects* — the margin over the negative controls is the evidence. It does not *rank* — and the ranking result is INCONCLUSIVE at n = 12, not refuted. Say inconclusive and mean it.

> **2 · The finding that carries the paper.** No method reproduces the pre-registered T > B ordering robustly -- across both reference builds and both cohorts -- against an instrument that shares nothing with the deconvolution arm. Say both references: none of twelve on the frozen signature; a few on the donor-level reference, of which the one consistent success (Bisque) is its reference's composition returned by the package's own declared assumption (Jew et al. 2020, Methods), shown on planted truth. The prediction was registered 95 minutes before the data existed and named its own falsifier. GBM is discovery; LGG is the registered replication in a different tumour type at 3.4x the sample size.

> **2c · A third instrument, at the protein level.** The pre-registered IMC test (§4.11) adds imaging mass cytometry -- through published per-marker-set correlations, not per-sample data -- to the two DNA instruments. It reaches the same verdict: ACS reversed the protein-measured ordering of two marker sets for one algorithm. Say plainly that this arm rests on another group's published correlations.

> **2b · A failure ACS cannot see, by construction.** ACS scores within-tumour contrasts, which depend only on how samples rank. Bisque without overlapping subjects keeps the ranking (planted-truth rho 0.88-0.97) and replaces the level with the reference's. That is a concrete, demonstrated instance of the thesis: anatomy detects some failures and is structurally blind to others.

> **2d · A truth-free check that does see the lymphoid failure (exploratory, §4.12).** Re-fitting one genuine package under different loss scales leaves tumour and total leukocyte content in place and moves the lymphoid total, and the compartments that stay put are the ones DNA confirms (rho = 0.89 across six units, p = 0.017). This sharpens the headline: the bulk data identify how much immune tissue there is, not which lymphocytes it holds. Say what it cannot do: T cells in GBM are stable (0.89) and do not track EpiDISH (-0.12), so the check flags what not to trust and certifies nothing -- though against GIMiCC the same estimate tracks (+0.64), so even this counter-example depends on which methylation truth is right. Six units, post-registration, one package for the stability arm.

> **3 · Where this sits in the field.** [4] reaches the same conclusion about pseudobulk benchmarks from a different direction and at 5,891 samples, which removes the obvious objection that our orthogonal arm is the broken one. But their criterion is *reproducibility* and ours is *correctness against an orthogonal instrument*: nothing in a reproducibility design can detect a method that is reproducibly wrong, which is exactly what we exhibit. `docs/RELATED_WORK.md` has the comparison table and the one genuine disagreement (BayesPrism). The 2024–2026 benchmarks that do have truth meet the same boundary: the DREAM challenge [47] finds coarse populations predicted well in purified-cell admixtures, with CD4+ T-cell subsets detectable only above about 6%; omnideconv [48] reports, against IHC in lung tumours, that "all methods struggled to robustly estimate tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes". Orthogonal truth in brain tissue exists for healthy cortex [49]; the truths here are DNA measurements in two glioma cohorts. §4.12 adds that the failure is visible without truth.

> **4 · What it means practically.** A published immune fraction for a glioma cannot be believed without an orthogonal measurement, and no internal check substitutes: the one that flags the lymphoid estimate (loss-scale stability, §4.12) says what not to trust, not what to trust. Connect this back to the equity argument from the Introduction: the labs that most need deconvolution are the least able to validate it, and this study does not solve that — it measures how far the cheapest available check gets you.

> **5 · What would settle the open question.** More comparable methods. With twelve, the registered test is underpowered: if anatomy tracked accuracy at a true rank correlation of 0.70 the criterion would be met in 65% of studies like this one, and at 0.80 in 83%. A true correlation exactly at the bar is met about half the time at any panel size (43%, 48%, 51%, 47% for 12, 20, 30, 50 methods), because the criterion thresholds the estimate at the bar itself. 80% power at a true 0.70 needs between 30 and 50 methods (77% at 30, 86% at 50) (simulation, `scripts/agreement_power.py`: a sensitivity power analysis for effects fixed in advance, not observed power). No reanalysis widens the panel; only more methods do.

## Limitations

> WRITE: all ten from `docs/PAPER_OUTLINE.md` §9, in the body. None in a footnote.

The two that a reviewer will find first: the **GBM per-type arm is n = 56** (most TCGA-GBM methylation is HM27, not HM450), and **one reference atlas** underlies every method, so "biology breaks deconvolution" cannot be fully separated from "the biology is under-represented in GBmap".

- **Survival could not be analysed.** Ivy GAP publishes survival times for 32 of 42 tumours and no vital status, so censoring is unknowable; the blanks are not random -- MGMT-methylated in 8/9 blank vs 9/31 recorded (Fisher p = 0.0021). The original prognostic aim is BLOCKED, not failed.
- **The reference's B-cell profile rests on few patients.** 1143 training B cells come from 31 donors, and three donors supply 78% of them.
- **Methylation is a cohort-level truth for the lymphoid split.** Its per-sample T/(T+B) failed a reference-free marker control (`results/lymphoid_tracking.json`); so did GIMiCC's, a second, glioma-specific methylation method (`results/gimicc_secondary.json`, Q4); per-sample statements describe methylation, not a validated per-sample truth.
- **The extension panel was added after registration** (§4.10) and enters no registered statistic; the IMC test (§4.11) rests on another group's published correlations, not per-sample data.
